title: Suman Lata Sengar v. State of U.P. — bill dispute relegated to clause 6.5
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: B. Amit Sthalekar, J.; Manju Rani Chauhan, J.
disposition: Writ dismissed; relegated to Executive Engineer under clause 6.5.
headnote: A writ seeking quashing of a demand notice of Rs. 76,137 towards electricity arrears was dismissed. A consumer who disputes an electricity bill and seeks its correction has a statutory remedy of approaching the Executive Engineer under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.
facts: Suman Lata Sengar petitioned the Allahabad High Court to quash a demand notice dated 24 November 2018 requiring payment of Rs. 76,137 as arrears of electricity. She disputed the bill and asked for its correction. Respondent no. 4 is the Executive Engineer, Electricity Distribution Division, Sirsaganj, District Firozabad. Counsel for the petitioner, for the licensee, and the Standing Counsel for the State were heard on 10 January 2019.

holding_units.holding: Where the petitioner disputes an electricity bill and seeks its correction, the remedy is to approach the Executive Engineer under clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; a writ petition to quash the demand notice is dismissed on that alternative remedy.

principle_tags.application: The Division Bench treated clause 6.5 as the statutory forum for a consumer disputing a bill and seeking correction, and dismissed the writ on that remedy.
The petitioner was directed to the Executive Engineer, Electricity Distribution Division, Sirsaganj, Firozabad, under clause 6.5 rather than to writ relief against the demand notice.
The challenge was to the correctness of an arrears demand of Rs. 76,137; that billing dispute was left to the Executive Engineer under clause 6.5.

not_decided.point: correctness of the demand of Rs. 76,137 and the electricity bill
not_decided.note: Left to the Executive Engineer under clause 6.5.
